bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide incentives for certain residential rental property.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9573 directly implicates IRS and the Office of Tax Policy, as any amendment to the Internal Revenue Code requires Treasury to interpret, regulate, and administer the new provisions. The implementation risk centers on drafting guidance, modeling revenue impact, and ensuring the incentive structure does not create unintended tax avoidance opportunities in the residential rental sector.

bills.title: Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 24 - 16.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7972 directly touches IRS workforce and human capital authorities under Treasury's tax administration umbrella, implicating the IRS's ability to hire, classify, and retain personnel. The implementation risk centers on potential disruptions to IRS modernization hiring pipelines and compliance with existing civil service and appropriations constraints during a period of ongoing IT and enforcement capacity build-out.

bills.title: Tax Exempt Hospital Transparency Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 25 - 15.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9504 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service's administration of section 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status for nonprofit hospitals, falling squarely within Treasury/IRS jurisdiction over exempt organization reporting and compliance. The bill's expanded Schedule H disclosure requirements and potential revocation triggers create significant IRS implementation burden and raise revenue-scoring implications that Treasury's Office of Tax Policy would need to analyze.

bills.title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9500 directly implicates IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code, likely touching the Office of Tax Policy and IRS Chief Counsel regarding the tax treatment of fraud-related losses or recoveries. The unanimity of the committee vote signals broad political momentum, raising implementation pressure on IRS to issue guidance and manage potential revenue cost risk against the baseline.

bills.title: Taxpayer Advocate Participation Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9498 directly implicates the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate (OTA) under IRC Section 7803(c), which sits within IRS and is subject to Treasury oversight. Treasury must monitor implementation risk around any expanded OTA participation rights that could constrain IRS enforcement discretion or create new procedural obligations affecting tax administration operations.

bills.title: End Tax Penalties on American Hostages Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9496 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would waive or abate tax penalties and interest for Americans who are wrongfully detained or held hostage abroad. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS operational burden to identify qualifying individuals, administer the relief mechanism, and address potential revenue loss scoring requirements.

bills.title: AI Tax Integrity Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus:
Without a known nexus provided, here is a placeholder briefing based on the bill title alone:

H.R. 9501 would direct IRS and potentially the Office of Tax Policy to establish standards governing AI use in tax administration and compliance determinations, implicating both Title 26 enforcement authority and Treasury's oversight of IRS operational systems. The unanimous committee vote signals near-certain floor advancement, requiring Treasury to assess implementation costs, rulemaking obligations, and legal liability risks tied to AI-driven tax decisions before the bill reaches the Senate.

bills.title: Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9499 directly implicates IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code to regulate paid tax return preparers, touching the IRS Return Preparer Office and potentially Treasury's broader regulatory authority following *Loving v. IRS*. The implementation risk centers on whether Treasury and IRS can enforce preparer identification and competency requirements without additional statutory authorization, and the unanimous committee vote signals strong legislative momentum requiring IRS to assess compliance infrastructure needs.

bills.title: Credit Access and Inclusion Act of 2025
bills.status: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 28 - 23.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5402 would amend the Fair Credit Reporting Act to allow utility and telecom payment data to be reported to credit bureaus, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Consumer Policy and its work on financial inclusion and credit access. The implementation risk centers on data accuracy standards and potential fair lending concerns that could draw interagency scrutiny from CFPB and the banking regulators Treasury coordinates with.

bills.title: Community Flood Resilience Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because the bill touches the Federal Insurance Office (FIO) and potentially the Federal Emergency Management Agency's flood insurance programs, which intersect with Treasury's role in monitoring systemic risk in insurance markets under the Dodd-Frank Act. The implementation angle centers on Treasury's exposure to fiscal risk if flood insurance obligations grow beyond program solvency, and FIO's mandate to assess gaps in insurance coverage that could destabilize broader financial markets.

bills.title: Expressing support for the work of open water lifeguards as first responders and emergency response providers.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
bills.nexus: H.Res. 1188 is a simple House resolution expressing symbolic support for open water lifeguards and carries no tax, financial regulatory, or appropriations provisions that would implicate any Treasury office or authority. Treasury has no implementation role or fiscal risk here, and no action or monitoring is warranted.

bills.title: Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7960 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would impose an excise tax on major integrated oil companies' quarterly profits exceeding a pre-pandemic baseline. Treasury must assess the revenue scoring, rulemaking burden on IRS to define and administer the windfall threshold, and the legal risk of constitutional or administrative challenges to a novel profits-based excise structure.

bills.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
bills.nexus: H.R. 7148 directly governs discretionary funding levels for the Department of the Treasury, including appropriations for IRS operations, the Office of Financial Research, and departmental offices such as OFAC and FinCEN. Treasury's implementation risk centers on operating under enacted spending caps that may constrain IRS enforcement staffing, technology modernization, and sanctions administration capacity for the full fiscal year.

bills.title: Helping Young Americans Save for Retirement Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4718 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would amend Internal Revenue Code provisions governing retirement plan eligibility, likely expanding access to tax-advantaged accounts for younger workers. The implementation risk centers on IRS guidance and regulatory updates needed to administer new eligibility rules, with potential revenue scoring implications that Treasury's Office of Tax Analysis would need to evaluate.
